shoal_e07_entry.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_entry.text: On Day Two Hundred Seventy-Four, Han paid the final twenty-five copper after reconciling Yue's thirty actual performed shifts. One hundred fifty copper was received in all. The restoration appropriation's actual expenditure was four hundred fifty-two, with twenty-eight unused care copper returned to its named source. The last account closed before a new practice offer was opened. Outside, Yue heard the yard's ordinary morning calls and felt the strange freedom of no longer being one of the people they summoned to work.

shoal_e07_setup_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_setup_01.text: The new practice offer came from the Outer Shoal Technical School, whose separately approved thirty-two-copper account funded a bounded local small-talisman test. Twelve paid the qualified examiner's defined preparation and two sessions, eight the independent technical supervisor's calibration and stop work, six actual consumables, and six ordinary care if needed. The school did not claim Yue's private bodily routes or promise advancement. It wanted to establish what one already earned sixth-stage practitioner could safely do in one local setup.

shoal_e07_setup_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_setup_02.text: Yue could refuse the offer after her paid labor term ended. She inspected its actual ground, ordinary exits, and available qualified care before agreeing to the narrow two-session scope. The first session would be on Day Two Hundred Seventy-Six. A later session depended on the stop record, ordinary assessment, and current recovery. Neither school nor examiner could call a damaged hand a useful cost of enlightenment. Yue signed that condition in her own words below the printed one.

shoal_e07_setup_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_setup_03.text: The examiner lived in the port and held current local qualifications for this scale of test. He was not a newly revealed ancestor, a distant patron arrived instantly from Lark, or the restoration supervisor transformed into a cultivation master. The technical supervisor controlled the external apparatus; the examiner assessed Yue's practice; the ordinary practitioner handled bodily care. They agreed on where each role stopped. Yue had to know whose instruction applied before she could obey it under strain.

shoal_e07_setup_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_setup_04.text: At the unpowered preparation table, the examiner read the Lark sixth-stage certificate as earned history. Six primary pairs remained hers. Today's application ceiling stayed half a unit over four ordinary breaths, a quarter useful work, independently stopped and grounded, with recovered throughput no greater than an eighth per breath. The new table's size did not enlarge that ceiling. He wrote the useful output on the apparatus card so nobody would confuse an attractive paper symbol with permission to power a room.

shoal_e07_setup_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_setup_05.text: The small talisman consisted of a port-school practice card with a bounded external trace, not a secret artifact taken from a salvage owner. Its task was to shift a light comparison marker through a calibrated short channel and then stop. No fuel socket was attached. The useful load stayed at the tested quarter-unit maximum, and the remainder would discharge into the measured ground path. A moved marker could establish that particular task; it could not certify a lamp, a boat, or an emergency shield.

shoal_e07_setup_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_setup_06.text: Yue practiced the release stroke without energy while the supervisor stood beyond her arm. His independent stop did not require her to remain conscious or attentive. He demonstrated its ordinary isolation under an unpowered test, then reset it visibly. The examiner asked what Yue would do if the supervisor called stop before she felt a problem. She would stop, report her own sensation, and let the record distinguish their observations. Feeling certain was not a reason to finish a prohibited breath.

shoal_e07_setup_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_setup_07.text: A student watching the dry preparation wanted to draw Yue's internal routes. She declined the request because the school needed the measured external setup, not her private bodily diagram. The student could draw the card's offered practice trace and apparatus. He accepted the smaller drawing and discovered that the ground path occupied more of his page than the pretty symbol. Yue liked the result. A useful instructional picture sometimes gave the least dramatic part the most space.

shoal_e07_setup_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_setup_08.text: Yan visited only to inspect the ordinary clear lane through the yard. He was not Yue's cultivation examiner. His crew would have an active lift at the far end during the planned session, so the school moved the observer line farther back and fixed a quiet signaling position. If the lift changed unexpectedly, the session would stop. The relocation cost setup time. It bought a boundary that a shouted instruction could cross without being mistaken for a rigger's command.

shoal_e07_setup_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_setup_09.text: The examiner asked about Yue's shoulder as a current condition rather than a character flaw she should conquer. She described the heat after long labeling and the existing waist clearance. The practice would be seated with her arm supported, and the ordinary grip check would come before any energy. The school could learn from a smaller setup. Yue could not learn safely from a setup that demanded more motion than her injured shoulder could actually bear.

shoal_e07_setup_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_setup_10.text: After preparation, Yue ate at a public stall and listened to two apprentices argue about whether a stopped trial counted as work. One said the marker had to reach the end to matter; the other said an early stop told them where a task failed. Yue asked whether they would prefer a finished bad measure or an unfinished useful one. They argued about that too. She left them the question rather than delivering a lesson the school had not hired her to teach.

shoal_e07_setup_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_setup_11.text: On Day Two Hundred Seventy-Five, the supervisor calibrated the light marker without Yue supplying energy. He used the school's named reference and recorded the unloaded conditions. The marker slid too easily on the first channel because someone had polished it beyond the specified surface. He replaced that channel before the session. A smooth movement would have looked impressive and measured the wrong task. Yue watched the correction from outside the setup and felt relieved by the ordinary suspicion of convenient results.

shoal_e07_setup_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_setup_12.text: The consumables allocation bought the permitted practice cards, ground-contact paper, and specified marker sleeves. It did not purchase a stock of stones or limitless fuel for later institutions. Unused ordinary materials remained school property. Yue would own her permitted practice notes, with the apparatus record held by the examiner under its stated scope. A simple local experiment had more owners than an audience might notice. They mattered because somebody would need to retrieve the right item when the table was cleared.

shoal_e07_setup_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_setup_13.text: The school announced a small observer capacity and left several interested people without places. Rong asked for a supplier seat and was refused because this practice was not a commercial freight-signal qualification. He could read the offered public result afterward. The disappointed student from the drawing table gained a place only when another student declined. Yue was glad no official treated her familiar face as a reason to expand the room until its ordinary exits ceased to work.

shoal_e07_setup_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_setup_14.text: At home that evening, she held her own practice strip between thumb and finger without loading it. The release motion had become familiar enough to make her careless in imagination. She pictured the marker moving cleanly and caught herself rehearsing the audience's relief rather than the actual stop. She put the strip down. Tomorrow's measured result would arrive through a body that needed sleep, not through the picture of competence she wanted other people to carry away.

shoal_e07_setup_15.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_setup_15.text: On the morning of Day Two Hundred Seventy-Six, the examiner checked touch, grip, leg stability, and current symptoms before permitting the supported waist-height setup. The checks matched the recorded clearance without certifying a sudden healed shoulder. Yue could do the small task today within its boundary. The supervisor reset the independent stop in her view and confirmed the ground contact. The observers settled. Nobody had promised a new stage, and the quiet room made that absence feel wonderfully ordinary.

shoal_e07_setup_16.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_setup_16.text: The first breath carried the preregistered eighth-unit maximum input into the measured setup. Yue kept her shoulder supported and watched the external marker rather than imagining a harbor light answering her. The marker advanced a short distance. The supervisor recorded the first reading independently. No one applauded. The examiner counted an ordinary breath pace, slow enough that Yue could hear it clearly. A quarter useful task had room to fail long before a large power would have begun to matter.

shoal_e07_setup_17.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_setup_17.text: On the second breath, the marker caught against a fine burr that the unloaded calibration had not exposed under this exact contact. Yue felt the urge to push harder. She recognized it just late enough that her fingers tightened around the supported edge. The supervisor called stop and isolated the apparatus through the independent mechanism. Yue completed her release stroke at once. The marker did not reach its endpoint. The test ended with measured input below the half-unit ceiling.

shoal_e07_setup_18.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_setup_18.text: The grounded remainder registered within the setup's planned bound. No qi spread across the yard or formed a wall against the sea. Yue's right fingertips tingled after the stopped contact, and her grip had changed. The examiner removed her from powered work and recorded the actual second-breath failure. He did not ask for a third breath to see whether the problem corrected itself. The apparatus could wait. A changed hand was a present bodily fact, not an obstacle to a good story.

shoal_e07_setup_19.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_setup_19.text: The ordinary practitioner examined Yue under the new practice care allocation. She described the onset and the remaining sensation without diagnosing it herself. He charged the accepted six-copper assessment and follow-up scope, advised rest, and prohibited another powered trial until the current checks cleared it. No potion restored a perfect hand in front of the observers. Yue felt angry that such a small task had exposed a limit. The anger did not alter its measured cost.

shoal_e07_setup_20.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_setup_20.text: At the apparatus, the supervisor found the contact burr under a qualified close inspection and preserved the faulty sleeve for the school record. His prior unloaded calibration had not made him blameless about every changed contact condition. He added the missed condition to his report. The examiner recorded Yue's late tightening separately. The failure had more than one contributing action. It would be wrong to give the whole burden to a talented operator or excuse her contribution because the tool also had a fault.

shoal_e07_setup_21.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_setup_21.text: The student who had drawn the ground path asked whether the sketch should show the failed marker position. The examiner said yes, with its actual date and setup condition. Yue permitted inclusion of the external stop sequence, excluding private bodily routes. The student added a second line where the marker had stalled. His picture became less symmetrical and more useful. The pretty symbol remained on the card, but the new educational point occupied the crooked place it had not crossed.

shoal_e07_setup_22.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_setup_22.text: Rong read the offered public stopped result and asked whether it was a poor advertisement for sixth-stage work. Yue said it was a result of one small local setup. Her stage remained earned, and this application remained stopped and unqualified until the current problem was addressed. He could neither market it as a success nor describe all cultivation as disproved by a burr. The merchant accepted the narrow answer more readily than she accepted it inside her own pride.

shoal_e07_setup_23.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_setup_23.text: Yan's crew passed the observer lane after their unrelated ordinary lift ended. One worker said the early stop sounded sensible; another wondered why they spent so much effort on a quarter-unit marker. The examiner answered the actual task question: this was a bounded local application test, not a source of harbor power. If the task's future value did not justify its cost, the school could stop funding it. Yue did not get to make it worthwhile by increasing the load on the next attempt.

shoal_e07_setup_24.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_setup_24.text: She left with a current restriction and a dated next-day assessment. The observers went back to classes, trade, or ordinary work. Some would remember the marker stuck; some would remember the stop. Yue would have to live with both memories without secretly performing a clean demonstration later. At the lodging door, she asked the keeper for the ordinary quiet hour and used her own paid room to rest. A stopped public failure had followed her home, and it was still survivable.

shoal_e07_recovery_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_recovery_01.text: On Day Two Hundred Seventy-Seven, Yue returned for the actual next-day check. The practitioner tested touch and grip, asked about leg stability and changed symptoms, and kept her off powered work because the tingling had not fully settled. Her shoulder remained limited to cleared waist tasks. The assessment's follow-up belonged to the already paid six-copper scope. A second appointment did not imply a second miracle or a second hidden bill paid by a closed restoration fund.

shoal_e07_recovery_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_recovery_02.text: She could walk the ordinary public route and do permitted light tasks with rest. The examiner set no resumption date by optimism. A later session on Day Two Hundred Eighty remained provisional until current checks cleared it. Yue went to the public beach again and disliked how little a walk seemed to accomplish. The dog that had chased foam was absent. Rest did not supply an entertaining replacement for the effort she had been told to stop.

shoal_e07_recovery_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_recovery_03.text: At a mending stall, a woman offered Yue a needle after seeing the loose cuff stitch. Yue said her hand had a current restriction and bought the ordinary repair instead. The mender charged the posted small fee and kept her own pace. A cultivator could need another person's craft without secretly studying it to surpass her. Yue watched the needle pass through the cloth and let the discomfort of receiving a simple service remain.

shoal_e07_recovery_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_recovery_04.text: That afternoon, Song Mei found her outside the public board and asked how the practice had gone. Yue said it had stopped and described the offered public facts, not the private clinical detail. The performer asked whether she wanted company or quiet. Yue chose a short walk. Song Mei did not tell her that failure would make her stronger. She complained about a room keeper who had tried to charge for a broken stool he had failed to inspect.

shoal_e07_recovery_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_recovery_05.text: They laughed about the keeper's proposed fee, then stopped laughing when Yue admitted she wanted another test simply to erase the audience's picture of the stuck marker. Song Mei said an audience could keep its picture. The performer still remembered the interrupted leaving piece without requiring every later performance to repair its exact ending. Yue did not find that comforting at first. It sounded like accepting a loss she wanted declared temporary.

shoal_e07_recovery_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_recovery_06.text: Song Mei asked what actually remained damaged. Yue named the changed hand sensation, the faulty sleeve, and the unqualified local task. Then she named her pride and realized it belonged in a different line. The artist did not make a lesson out of her pause. They watched a merchant argue with a boy carrying pears and went their separate ways when the walk's agreed time ended. Yue could recover without making every friend supervise the recovery.

shoal_e07_recovery_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_recovery_07.text: On Day Two Hundred Seventy-Eight, the supervisor brought the corrected external contact design to the school board. He had changed the sleeve inspection to include the condition that revealed the burr and retained the failed piece for comparison. The revision was a new documented setup, not a claim that the original apparatus had always been sound. Students could compare the two permitted external traces. Yue's bodily routes remained unoffered and absent from both.

shoal_e07_recovery_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_recovery_08.text: One student wanted to keep the failed marker sleeve as a personal lucky charm. The school declined because the piece was retained school property in a fault record, and a potentially misleading working shape should not circulate as an unexplained object. The student settled for a permitted drawing. Yue smiled at the familiar urge to turn an ugly result into a meaningful token. The retained sleeve could be useful without belonging to whoever liked its story.

shoal_e07_recovery_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_recovery_09.text: The examiner asked whether Yue wanted the corrected local test to continue if the hand checks cleared it. She said yes for the specific small task, not to make the earlier failure disappear. He wrote the reason in her accepted practice note. Her statement could be wrong in private feeling and still guide a better action. The second session would remain a fresh dated trial with its own stop, independent calibration, measured input, and ordinary next-day review.

shoal_e07_recovery_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_recovery_10.text: On Day Two Hundred Seventy-Nine, the practitioner found the fingertip sensation had settled to its prior baseline under ordinary rest. Touch, grip, and leg checks matched the narrow permitted setup. He retained the shoulder's waist-work restriction and advised ending a trial on any recurrence. This was permission for the supported local task, not proof of full healing. Yue felt relief and kept the written restriction instead of quietly putting it beneath the more flattering certificate.

shoal_e07_recovery_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_recovery_11.text: That evening, the school held a brief planning meeting about communicating stopped work. Public workers had heard that the apparatus failed; some students had heard that Yue failed; a supplier had heard that the useful load was too small to matter. Each version omitted a different fact. The offered public record could be shared in a bounded form. It would not include her private clinical history or supply a verdict on every similar device in the port.

shoal_e07_recovery_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_recovery_12.text: The new Learned Stops Communication Allowance offered eight copper for one defined public distribution. One route could print sixteen school diagrams of the permitted external setup and stopped sequence, with six for copying and two for messages. Another could translate ordinary stop instructions for new workers and print eight cards, with four for the translator, two for copying, and two for messages. The audiences and detail would differ; the allowance could not purchase both batches.

shoal_e07_recovery_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_recovery_13.text: The ordinary stop cards would not teach cultivation or certify a device. They would explain the worker's allowed signal, clear route, and current receiving contact in the requested language. The diagrams would show more apparatus detail to readers attending the school, without translated street instructions. The relevant workers had requested the language service, and school visitors had requested the picture. Yue could support the offered distribution she found most useful, while its authors retained approval of their own text.

shoal_e07_recovery_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_recovery_14.text: Rong wanted a supplier advertisement added to either batch. The communication source declined because this allowance funded a stopped-test explanation or ordinary stop instructions, not a commercial endorsement. He agreed to submit a separate offered sponsorship proposal later if one was wanted. Yue had expected the refusal to become an argument. Sometimes a narrow account made it easier for a merchant to hear no, because he could see precisely which work he had asked it to become.

shoal_e07_recovery_15.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_recovery_15.text: Before choosing, she checked that neither batch would imply the corrected trial had already succeeded. The diagrams would carry the actual stopped result and date. The translated cards would carry ordinary action instructions, not an image of Yue as their guarantor. The second trial remained tomorrow's event. She would not let useful public communication move it into yesterday's success column. The allowance's small size made the missing audience concrete without making either offered audience less deserving.

shoal_e07_instruction_choice.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_instruction_choice.text: The eight-copper allowance could serve one requested audience now. Sixteen school diagrams would show the measured stopped setup in greater detail, but remain in the common reading language. Eight translated ordinary stop cards would reach new workers who requested that language, but omit the apparatus explanation. Neither included Yue's private routes or promised a successful future trial. She chose which offered distribution to support.

choices.text: Support the sixteen permitted school diagrams.
Support the eight translated ordinary stop cards.

shoal_e07_school_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_school_01.text: The school copy worker laid the offered external diagram beside the actual stopped-trial record. Yue checked that the marker's failed position had survived the reduction to a small page. The supervisor checked the independent stop and ground labels. The examiner checked the measured input wording. Each approved only the part he could verify. Six copper paid the actual sixteen-copy run. The student whose first sketch had favored the pretty symbol saw the crooked stopped line at the center of the new sheet.

shoal_e07_school_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_school_02.text: The two-copper message work carried the finished copies to the specified school notice and lesson desks. A receipt established delivery, not that sixteen readers had absorbed them. The school posted its public hours, including a later slot workers could attend if their own jobs allowed it. No translator had been employed under this route. People needing the requested second language would have to receive a separately offered service later; this batch could not claim to have reached them.

shoal_e07_school_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_school_03.text: At the first public reading, a student asked why the operator's late tightening and the tool's burr appeared together. The examiner said the result had both observed contributions. Showing only one would make a cleaner accusation and a worse lesson. Yue answered one offered question about the release timing while leaving her clinical detail private. The student revised his own sketch. A diagram could let an ordinary reader ask a sharper question without making him an examiner overnight.

shoal_e07_school_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_school_04.text: A supplier hand attending after work wanted to know whether the drawing applied to his employer's fueled signal device. The supervisor said the illustrated setup was unpowered except for the bounded practice input and did not qualify that other device. The man took the permitted sheet to his employer as a question, not a safety certificate. Yue watched the public explanation leave the room with a useful limit still attached. Whether that limit survived later telling would need a current check.

shoal_e07_school_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_school_05.text: The workers who had requested translated cards received an actual notice that this allowance had funded the school diagrams instead. Their request remained unperformed, and the public gate's existing ordinary instruction process remained in force. He Ming offered to bring a later translation proposal through the normal source, with no guaranteed approval. Yue could support it later but could not count a future hope as eight completed cards tonight.

shoal_e07_school_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_school_06.text: The allowance closed after sixteen actual copies and the specified messages, eight copper spent. Yue retained no private teaching mandate or ownership of the student's original sketch. The school diagrams now gave common-language readers a detailed external failure sequence. They did not reach the unserved language audience merely because anyone could enter a public room. That omission would shape the next dispute differently from the missing apparatus detail on the alternative cards.

shoal_e07_signs_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_signs_01.text: The requested-language worker met the translator at a public table and chose the terms she would actually use in a shouted stop. Yue described the ordinary action sequence without pretending to know the language's distinctions herself. The translator explained one ambiguous word that could mean wait rather than end the task. They selected a phrase the worker recognized and checked its meaning back through the common language before the text was approved.

shoal_e07_signs_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_signs_02.text: Four copper paid the translator's actual agreed task. Two paid eight ordinary cards carrying the stop signal, clear route, and current receiving contact. Two paid their specified delivery messages to the workers' public instruction desks. The cards did not teach Yue's internal routes, describe a fueled device as safe, or claim tomorrow's trial had succeeded. The relevant supervisor approved the action content while the translator retained responsibility for the offered language.

shoal_e07_signs_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_signs_03.text: At a quiet instruction interval, workers who had requested the language practiced the ordinary signal without any active load. One called it too softly to carry across the marked safe route, and the instructor asked for a clearer ordinary voice. Yue stood among observers rather than taking over the lesson. Her small failed trial had supplied an example of why a stop mattered; it did not qualify her to supervise every worker who now held a translated card.

shoal_e07_signs_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_signs_04.text: A worker asked whether shouting the printed phrase made the apparatus stop automatically. The instructor said the ordinary supervisor still had to operate the independent mechanism or the worker's assigned release where applicable. A word was an instruction inside a staffed arrangement, not a spell. They rehearsed who heard and who acted at the actual desk. The cards became useful through people who could perform those roles, not through the name of a sixth-stage visitor on the story that had prompted them.

shoal_e07_signs_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_signs_05.text: The school visitors who wanted detailed diagrams received a public notice that this allowance had funded the translated cards instead. The offered stopped-trial record remained available at the existing school desk, but no sixteen-copy illustrated batch had been made. A student could attend and ask under those hours; he could not take a distributed picture that did not exist. Yue accepted the missing detail as a real consequence of serving the requested language audience.

shoal_e07_signs_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_signs_06.text: The allowance closed after the actual translation, eight printed cards, and specified messages, eight copper spent. New workers had a current ordinary instruction in the requested language. The broader school audience lacked a portable picture of the apparatus fault. Neither absence would be quietly filled from Yue's personal purse to make the selection disappear. The next public dispute would begin with different shared knowledge depending on which audience had actually received the work.

shoal_e07_trial_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_trial_01.text: On Day Two Hundred Eighty, the second session began with a new dated calibration, not the first session's corrected page reused as proof. The supervisor checked the revised sleeve under the current permitted contact condition. The examiner checked Yue's touch, grip, legs, symptoms, and ordinary rest. The supporting surface stood at its declared waist height. The independent stop and measured ground were tested before her input. A clean setup could be prepared; a clean result still had to happen.

shoal_e07_trial_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_trial_02.text: The corrected sleeve had a duller edge than the first one. Yue found it less beautiful and more comfortable beneath the permitted support. The student who had drawn the first setup wanted to shade it differently. The examiner allowed the offered exterior drawing after the trial, when nobody would be distracted by his pencil moving close to the table. Even a harmless-looking observer task had a time and a place. Yue waited until the student stepped back.

shoal_e07_trial_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_trial_03.text: The supervisor called the setup ready. Yue said aloud that she would stop on his instruction before trying to complete a reluctant movement. The examiner asked her to repeat the actual useful task, and she named the short marker channel and quarter-unit maximum. She did not name a clinic lamp or harbor gate. The words felt small. They gave her a place to put ambition without letting it decide the load.

shoal_e07_trial_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_trial_04.text: The first ordinary breath supplied no more than an eighth unit, recorded by the independent reference. The marker moved within its expected first interval. Yue kept her shoulder supported and her grip light. She could hear the examiner counting from beyond her immediate sight. The sound helped distinguish a measured pace from the quicker rhythm her excitement wanted. No one called her gifted while she was working. The room offered a count, a stop, and space.

shoal_e07_trial_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_trial_05.text: On the second breath, the marker crossed the position where the earlier sleeve had caught. Yue wanted to celebrate before the task was over. She kept her fingers relaxed and her attention on the current channel. The supervisor's hand remained at the independent isolation. Passing one former fault was a current observation, not proof that the next two breaths were safe. The earlier tingling had made this restraint feel bodily rather than merely virtuous.

shoal_e07_trial_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_trial_06.text: The third breath carried the marker through the next interval without exceeding the registered input. The ground reading remained within its planned bound. Yue did not speed up to make the final movement feel decisive. She could feel ordinary effort and a rising desire to finish. Neither sensation was ignored; neither established an emergency by itself. The examiner asked for her current response in the agreed short words, and she answered that it matched the permitted range.

shoal_e07_trial_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_trial_07.text: On the fourth ordinary breath, the marker reached the short channel's endpoint. The supervisor called the planned end, and Yue completed the release stroke without trying to keep the effect alive. Total measured input was half a unit, useful task a quarter, with the remainder registered in the bounded ground path. No fifth breath followed. The small talisman stopped. It had moved a light marker in one corrected local setup, not acquired a harbor's work by implication.

shoal_e07_trial_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_trial_08.text: The examiner checked immediate grip and sensation before anybody approached the table. Yue reported ordinary fatigue without renewed fingertip tingling. Her shoulder remained within its supported task condition. The supervisor recorded the independent end and ground readings separately. They did not award another cultivation stage. Six earned primary pairs stayed six, and the successful small application stayed local to its tested load, range, duration, and setup. Further questions would need further qualified work.

shoal_e07_trial_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_trial_09.text: The student asked whether he could erase the first failed picture now that the marker had reached the end. The examiner said no. Both dated results belonged in the offered record. The revision had succeeded under changed inspected conditions, which was why the failed condition still mattered. Yue felt the old wish to keep only the flattering image and declined it with him. A second result could improve her knowledge without replacing the first day that had taught her to stop.

shoal_e07_trial_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_trial_10.text: Rong received the public local result through the same ordinary desk as other interested readers. He asked whether it justified using a small talisman on freight signals. The supervisor said this particular marker task did not qualify a fueled application. The result might support a future bounded research proposal, not a working order. Rong wrote the distinction in his own note. He was learning how many promising measurements could precede one usable commercial device.

shoal_e07_trial_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_trial_11.text: Yan watched the apparatus be cleared before his crew's later movement resumed through the lane. He said the useful quarter sounded modest beside a loaded spar. Yue agreed because it was modest. Her circulation had a different task and ceiling. She could still hold an ordinary door, sort returned parts, or give a narrow witnessed account without making her energy large enough to impress a rigger. The thought felt less defensive after a measured small success than after an imagined one.

shoal_e07_trial_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_trial_12.text: The examiner prescribed ordinary rest and a next-day check before this local task could be treated as completed practice with recovery observed. Yue did not conduct another private repetition that evening. A successful four-breath sequence had consumed its measured effort and attention. Recovered throughput remained no greater than an eighth per ordinary breath under the established ceiling. The harbor's lamp line did not become her refillable battery because she had finally moved one marker cleanly.

shoal_e07_trial_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_trial_13.text: She walked the permitted public beach route with a tired body and no need to explain it to spectators. The dog returned this time, chasing a stick its owner threw well away from the water's dangerous edge. It brought back a different piece of driftwood and looked satisfied. Yue laughed, then checked the time before the lodging door closed. She could carry a modest success home without assigning the sea an opinion about it.

shoal_e07_trial_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_trial_14.text: On Day Two Hundred Eighty-One, the practitioner performed the scheduled next-day touch, grip, leg, and symptom checks. They matched the permitted baseline, with no return of the earlier fingertip change. The shoulder's waist clearance remained narrow; overhead work was still excluded. He closed the actual assessment and follow-up under its accepted six-copper scope. Recovery had been observed on a later date. It had not changed her history into a body that could no longer be hurt.

shoal_e07_trial_15.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_trial_15.text: The examiner filed the two dated trials and their separate current checks. The technical supervisor filed the independent calibrations, stops, ground readings, and changed contact condition. The failed sleeve stayed with the school record. The corrected apparatus stayed school property. Yue retained her permission-bounded personal notes. The school account's thirty-two copper paid the actual accepted examiner, supervisor, consumables, and care. The separately spent eight-copper communication account stayed separate.

shoal_e07_trial_16.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_trial_16.text: At the gate, an apprentice asked Yue how many units she would need to hold back a storm. She said she had no qualified application for that task. The small marker result gave no basis for the claim. The apprentice looked at the gray water and said an ordinary wall also seemed too small. Yue agreed that walls needed qualified design, maintenance, and limits too. The conversation could recognize fear without inventing a power large enough to dismiss it.

shoal_e07_trial_17.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_trial_17.text: She returned the last borrowed pencil to the school clerk. Its point had broken, and she told him before he could issue it to another student. He sharpened it with an ordinary knife. The humble correction pleased her more than it should have. A completed test still left a tool needing attention. People who worked after her would meet the actual pencil, not the clean story of her careful practice. She stayed until he checked its usable point.

shoal_e07_trial_18.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_trial_18.text: Outside, a clinic messenger stood by the receiving board asking about a medicine cargo that had not arrived on its estimated date. Its shared carrier had been delayed, and the fuel delivery connected to a later maintenance session had a different delay. The messenger needed actual receiving states rather than rumors. Yue recognized the distinctions before knowing the cargo's contents. A stopped local task could help her listen carefully without making her qualified to replace what the clinic lacked.

shoal_e07_trial_19.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_trial_19.text: The messenger had not asked Yue to practice on a patient or power a treatment room. He wanted the public location of the supplier's current receiving desk. She showed him on the current lane map and offered to accompany him only as far as the licensed public route. The ordinary practitioner would decide care with actual available supplies. Useful directions were a smaller help than a miracle, and the messenger accepted them without demanding the larger one.

shoal_e07_trial_20.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_trial_20.text: At the receiving desk, they found a request entered and a carrier delay noted, with no completed delivery mark. The clerk was not hiding a crate behind the wall. He could show the current public schedule and name the party permitted to update it. Yue heard the messenger count the days until his clinic's next posted work interval. Time had become an object he needed and could not buy simply by asking the question more urgently.

shoal_e07_trial_21.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_trial_21.text: She did not charge the closed practice account for this walk or promise another funded role. The messenger would return to his own employer with the public facts. If the clinic and supplier wanted a bounded follow-up task, they would offer its actual scope. Yue had finished the local small-talisman work at sixth stage with measured limits and recovery. A port supply delay now presented a different problem, made sharper by the fact that she could not solve it with that success.

shoal_e07_trial_22.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_trial_22.text: The sea wind lifted the current delay notice, and the clerk fastened its lower corner so the time remained readable. Yue held the paper while he worked. The gesture required ordinary fingers, currently checked and still limited. Beyond the receiving yard, someone called for a late boat that did not appear. She looked toward the lane the clinic messenger would take and understood that the next work would begin with an absence everybody wanted explained.

shoal_e07_exit.speaker: narrator
shoal_e07_exit.text: The messenger bought a bread heel before returning to the clinic. He had missed his own breakfast while checking the delayed cargo. Yue bought one too, and they ate beside the public wall, saying nothing that could make a late shared boat arrive sooner.
